title: Momotarō, the Peach Boy
place: Rural Japan and an island beyond the sea
note: A shortened new adaptation of Ozaki’s “Momotaro, or the Story of the Son of a Peach.” Violent details and imperial language in the historical edition are softened; oni are presented as folktale beings rather than people.

rights.basis: The 1908 source edition is identified as public domain in the United States by Project Gutenberg.

artLabel: Momotarō carries a banner beside a dog, monkey, and pheasant under a peach tree.

pageArt.alt: Momotarō shares millet dumplings with Dog, Monkey, and Pheasant on a rural Japanese road.
Momotarō and his animal companions sail home to a welcome beneath flowering peach branches.

scenes: An old woman washing clothes saw an enormous peach floating down the river. She carried it home to share with her husband.
When they cut it open, a healthy baby boy appeared. They named him Momotarō—Peach Boy.
Momotarō grew strong and kind. Hearing that oni on a distant island had stolen from nearby villages, he resolved to recover what they had taken.
His parents packed millet dumplings for the journey.
Along the road, Momotarō shared dumplings with a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant. Each promised to help, though first the three had to learn to work together.
At the island, Pheasant flew over the gate, Monkey climbed the wall, and Dog found the safest path. Their different gifts made one brave team.
The oni returned the stolen treasure and promised peace. Momotarō and his companions sailed home, where the old couple welcomed all four beneath the peach blossoms.
